quote: So to be honest, Tracy, I do think that you don't have enough sun for solely for solar to work for you, unfortunately.
stewart_read: The rep renders a hard-sounding DQ within the first 75 seconds of the call, before any verify-section item is confirmed, based solely on a satellite image read. This is a fast, confident DQ on a thin evidentiary basis (an admittedly obscured aerial photo) rather than a documented protocol for shade/tree DQs.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: the rep may be following a real internal policy that heavy tree coverage is an immediate hard-stop regardless of other qualifiers, making the fast DQ appropriate and efficient. However, no such policy is stated on the call, and the rep never explains any threshold (e.g., percentage shade, hours of direct sun) to Tracy or to us — so this can't be confirmed as principled vs. reactive.
coaching_implication: Confirm with Kenny whether shade/tree DQ has a defined threshold and whether reps are trained to at least complete the verify section (or offer a specialist shade assessment) before delivering a DQ, especially on an engaged inbound lead.

quote: It's just kinda hard to see because on Google Maps, all the trees are in the way.
stewart_read: The rep admits the tool he's using to make the DQ decision (Google Maps aerial imagery) is obscured by the very trees in question, yet proceeds to use it as the basis for the disqualification anyway rather than flagging uncertainty or offering a live assessment.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to acknowledge image limitations explicitly to the customer and offer an alternative verification path (specialist site visit, photo from customer) rather than DQ'ing on a tool the rep concedes is unreliable.

quote: I was looking at we have a a detached garage. Okay. Is that possible to put it out there at the garage?
schema_reference: cross_sell_signals.roof_replacement_planned (structural analog — customer proactively offering property alternatives)
stewart_read: Tracy is actively problem-solving to make solar work on her property, offering a detached garage as an alternative site. This is a highly engaged customer generating her own solution paths rather than accepting the first no.
coaching_implication: This customer's persistence is a signal worth flagging in coaching: reps should match this kind of proactive customer energy with equally thorough investigation (e.g., asking for photos, offering to escalate) rather than closing the door with the same brief reasoning used on the first structure.

quote: Kind of the same thing. I do think that you have too much shade. These solar panels, they need as much sun as they can get.
stewart_read: Rather than exploring specifics (how many hours of direct sun the garage gets, its orientation, or offering a professional shade study), the rep repeats a generic solar-panel-sun-need explanation and closes the option. No question was asked back to Tracy to gather any real data about the garage's exposure.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: the rep may simply lack a tool or process for verifying shade beyond the satellite view, so repeating the same reasoning is the only move available to them given their resources. This is the more supported read — there's no evidence the rep has access to sun-hours data.
coaching_implication: If reps only have access to satellite imagery, that's a tooling gap for Kenny to address — reps need either a shade-analysis tool or clear escalation path for edge cases like a detached structure with different sun exposure than the main roof.

quote: Now the wintertime, it would work perfectly because, like, right now, the sun is shining so brightly into this room.
stewart_read: Tracy gives the rep a specific, real-time observation (direct sun into her room right now) that contradicts the satellite-derived shade conclusion. The rep does not engage with this contradiction or ask a clarifying follow-up (time of day, which side of the house, season) — it's acknowledged with a flat 'Mhmm. Okay.' at 02:27 and then the DQ is simply repeated.
coaching_implication: Train reps to treat direct customer testimony about sun exposure as data to probe, not something to nod past — a specific follow-up question here could have surfaced information the satellite image couldn't show.

quote: Okay. So for ground mounted systems, we don't offer them just because due to trenching and everything involved. They do tend to get super, super expensive.
stewart_read: The rep volunteers a detailed cost/engineering rationale (trenching costs, why ground-mount isn't offered) that is closer-tier financial/technical content, rather than using the universal escape hatch to defer this explanation to a specialist while still capturing basic info.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: since ground-mount is apparently a hard no regardless of qualification, the rep may be closing this path quickly and accurately to save time on a genuinely unavailable option. This is plausible but the depth of unprompted cost explanation still exceeds what's needed to say 'we don't do ground-mount.'
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to give the bottom-line answer briefly ('we don't offer ground-mount systems') without volunteering the full cost/trenching rationale — keeps the call efficient and avoids sounding like a rep justifying company policy under mild challenge.

quote: But as of right now, we're we're not able. Yeah. I don't think that's what she's gonna do. Okay. Thank you.
stewart_read: The call ends abruptly with no recap, no note of what would need to change (e.g., 'if you do get those trees cleared, call us back and we'll take another look'), and no capture of any qualifying info that could make this lead reusable later (bill, utility company, interest reason).
coaching_implication: Even on a DQ, reps should close with a clear reopening path stated to the customer and logged for the CRM ('if the tree situation changes, here's how to reach us') rather than ending on a flat thank-you with nothing captured.
